Article 12

The Regional Government shall provide Women Protection in the form of:
a. prevention of Violence against Women;
b. provision of services for Women victims of Violence requiring coordination at the Regional level; and
c. strengthening and developing institutions providing Women Protection services.

Article 43

1. Every Child who is a victim of physical and/or psychological Violence as referred to in Article 36 letter g shall receive rehabilitation services both physical and psychosocial.
2. Forms of protection for Children who are victims of acts of Violence include basic social services, education, religious guidance, health services, psychological counseling and/or psychotherapy, legal assistance, recreational and educational activities and empowerment of parents of Children who are victims of acts of violence.
3. Every person and/or any party is prohibited from committing acts of Violence against Children.

Article 4

The regulation regarding Women Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:
a. guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of every Woman and Child to survival, growth and development;
b. improve the quality of life of Women, Children and family quality;
c. enhance institutional capacity for Women Empowerment and Child Protection in the Region, including the development of gender and Child data systems; and
d. provide protection of Women's rights and fulfillment of Children's Rights including Special Protection for Children from various forms of Violence and other discriminatory treatment.
1. Implementation

CHAPTER VII SAFE HOUSES

Article 46

1. Women and Children who are victims of Violence requiring ongoing handling have the right to stay in a safe house.
2. The safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall provide a temporary safe place or shelter for victims of Violence until the victim's rights are restored. (3) The operation and management of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that performs functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
4. Further provisions regarding the operation of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 45

1. Special Protection for Children who are victims of mistreatment and neglect as referred to in Article 36 letter i shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment and rehabilitation.
2. Every person and/or any party is prohibited from placing, allowing, involving, ordering the involvement of Children in situations of mistreatment and neglect as referred to in paragraph (1).

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tanah Bumbu Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Head of Region hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Tanah Bumbu Regency. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the people's representative institution of Tanah Bumbu Regency Region. 5. Agency is the Regional Apparatus that organizes government affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection. 6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in organizing government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that Women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 8. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into men and Women. 9. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person recognized by law as a Woman. 10. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a Child who is still in the womb. 11. Child in conflict with the law (ABH) is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child who is a victim of a criminal act and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 13. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting Women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security. 16. Toddler is a Child aged 0 (zero) to 5 (five) years, in the early stages of human development. 17. School-Age Child is a Child aged 6 (six) to 18 (eighteen) years. 18. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs for mental and religious guidance as well as clothing, food, shelter, health, education, physical, and social services are not properly met. 19. Child who is a victim of Violence is a Child who experiences mistreatment such as being abused, humiliated, which endangers the Child physically, mentally and socially. 20. Child maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over the child, who should be trusted, namely parents, close family, teachers, supervisors, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions (World Health Organization). 21. Child in emergency situation is a Child who is in a situation and condition that endangers them such as a Child victim of riots, a Child who becomes a refugee, a Child victim of natural disasters and a Child in armed conflict. 22. Child in conflict with the law is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child victim of a criminal act, and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 23. Child of isolated indigenous community is a Child who lives in a situation of isolation where they cannot access basic needs. 24. Economically exploited Child is a Child who is forced and/or deceived to be employed by parents or others, whether unpaid or paid. 25. Sexually exploited Child is the use of a Child for sexual purposes with cash or other forms of compensation between the Child, buyer of sexual services, intermediary or agent and other parties who profit from the sexual trade of the Child. 26. Child who is a victim of Napza abuse is a Child who suffers from dependence on Napza caused by Napza abuse, either by their own will or because of encouragement or coercion by others. 27. Child with special needs is a Child who experiences physical and/or mental disabilities that interfere with growth and development in accordance with the stages of Child development. 28. Child victim of maltreatment is a Child who receives treatment that is not in accordance with the rights of the Child. 29. Village is a legal Community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage Government affairs, the interests of the local Community, based on Community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights recognized and respected in the Government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 30. Child in need of Special Protection is a Child in an emergency situation, a Child in conflict with the law, a Child from an isolated indigenous community, a Child who is economically and/or sexually exploited, a Child victim of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other active substance abuse (Napza), a Child victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, a Child victim of physical and/or psychological Violence, a Child with special needs, and a Child victim of maltreatment and neglect. 31. Child Trafficking is a criminal act or action that meets one or more elements of recruitment, transfer, handover of a Child by using Violence or threat of violence, fraud, kidnapping, confinement, abuse of power, exploitation of a position of vulnerability or debt bondage for the purpose and/or resulting in exploiting the Child. 32.

Legal assistance/expert witness services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter d number 3 include:

a. ensuring the Child is accompanied by legal counsel; and

Article 40

1. Special Protection for Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 36 letter d shall be carried out through:
a. prevention of Children from being utilized by certain parties as objects of exploitation through supervision;
b. disseminating and/or socializing laws and regulations related to Protection of Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually;
c. monitoring, reporting and imposing sanctions; and
d. involving various government agencies, companies, labor unions, NGOs, and the Community in the elimination of exploitation of Children.
2. Every person and/or any party is prohibited from conducting economic and/or sexual exploitation of Children as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 25

1. Rescue actions as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b shall be carried out if based on the results of identification it is known that the safety of the Child is threatened.
2. Actions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by removing the Child from the threatening situation and environment.
3. The SKPD responsible for Child Protection affairs must carry out rescue actions and coordinate with the Police Apparatus/Civil Service Police Unit.

Part Eight

Protection of Children Requiring Special Protection

Article 42

1. Special Protection for Children who are victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking as referred to in Article 36 letter f shall be carried out through supervision, protection, prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and reintegration efforts by the Regional Government and the Community.
2. To implement prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government together with the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, Community, NGOs and Social Organizations shall take steps in the form of:
a. conducting socialization and/or campaigns on the prevention, handling and elimination of Child Trafficking practices;
b. conducting cooperation with other Regions as well as with other countries through bilateral or multilateral cooperation in accordance with the laws and regulations.
3. Protection for Children who are victims of Child Trafficking shall be implemented through Shelters and/or other Child Protection Institutions, through referrals from government institutions or the Community.
4. Every Child who is a victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, has the right to obtain physical, psychological treatment and rehabilitation and reintegration in the family environment and the Community.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by "respect for human rights" is that the protection and empowerment of women is carried out as a manifestation of respect for women as part of Human Rights.

Point b rights What is meant by "gender equality" is one of the basic rights as a human being, the right to live with dignity, free from fear and free to determine life choices is not only intended for men, women also have the same rights in essence.

Point c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward Children by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups, and the condition of the Child.

Point d What is meant by "justice and legal certainty" is that in implementing the protection and empowerment of women it is based on justice and legal certainty of equality between men and women. Point e What is meant by "benefit" is to provide the widest possible benefit for children and women for the interests of society, nation and state.

Point f What is meant by "participatory" is that every member of society is encouraged to play an active role in the decision-making process and implementation of child protection and women's empowerment, either directly or indirectly.

Point g What is meant by "the best interests of the Child" is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the Regional Government, parents/family, and the Community, the best interests of the Child must be the primary consideration.

Child who is a victim of Violence is a Child who experiences mistreatment such as being abused, humiliated, which endangers the Child physically, mentally and socially. 20. Child of isolated indigenous community is a Child who lives in a situation of isolation where they cannot access basic needs. 24. Economically exploited Child is a Child who is forced and/or deceived to be employed by parents or others, whether unpaid or paid. 25. Sexually exploited Child is the use of a Child for sexual purposes with cash or other forms of compensation between the Child, buyer of sexual services, intermediary or agent and other parties who profit from the sexual trade of the Child. 26. Child who is a victim of Napza abuse is a Child who suffers from dependence on Napza caused by Napza abuse, either by their own will or because of encouragement or coercion by others. 27. Child with special needs is a Child who experiences physical and/or mental disabilities that interfere with growth and development in accordance with the stages of Child development. 28. Child victim of maltreatment is a Child who receives treatment that is not in accordance with the rights of the Child. 29. Village is a legal Community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage Government affairs, the interests of the local Community, based on Community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights recognized and respected in the Government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 30. Child in need of Special Protection is a Child in an emergency situation, a Child in conflict with the law, a Child from an isolated indigenous community, a Child who is economically and/or sexually exploited, a Child victim of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other active substance abuse (Napza), a Child victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, a Child victim of physical and/or psychological Violence, a Child with special needs, and a Child victim of maltreatment and neglect. 31. b. improve the quality of life of Women, Children and family quality;

Point a What is meant by "respect for human rights" is that the protection and empowerment of women is carried out as a manifestation of respect for women as part of Human Rights.

REGIONAL

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION. CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tanah Bumbu Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Head of Region hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Tanah Bumbu Regency. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the people's representative institution of Tanah Bumbu Regency Region. 5. Agency is the Regional Apparatus that organizes government affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection. 6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in organizing government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that Women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 8. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into men and Women. 9. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person recognized by law as a Woman. 10. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a Child who is still in the womb. 11. Child in conflict with the law (ABH) is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child who is a victim of a criminal act and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 13. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting Women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security. 16. Toddler is a Child aged 0 (zero) to 5 (five) years, in the early stages of human development. 17. School-Age Child is a Child aged 6 (six) to 18 (eighteen) years. 18. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs for mental and religious guidance as well as clothing, food, shelter, health, education, physical, and social services are not properly met. 19. Child who is a victim of Violence is a Child who experiences mistreatment such as being abused, humiliated, which endangers the Child physically, mentally and socially. 20. Child maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over the child, who should be trusted, namely parents, close family, teachers, supervisors, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions (World Health Organization). 21. Child in emergency situation is a Child who is in a situation and condition that endangers them such as a Child victim of riots, a Child who becomes a refugee, a Child victim of natural disasters and a Child in armed conflict. 22. Child in conflict with the law is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child victim of a criminal act, and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 23. Child of isolated indigenous community is a Child who lives in a situation of isolation where they cannot access basic needs. 24. Economically exploited Child is a Child who is forced and/or deceived to be employed by parents or others, whether unpaid or paid. 25. Sexually exploited Child is the use of a Child for sexual purposes with cash or other forms of compensation between the Child, buyer of sexual services, intermediary or agent and other parties who profit from the sexual trade of the Child. 26. Child who is a victim of Napza abuse is a Child who suffers from dependence on Napza caused by Napza abuse, either by their own will or because of encouragement or coercion by others. 27. Child with special needs is a Child who experiences physical and/or mental disabilities that interfere with growth and development in accordance with the stages of Child development. 28. Child victim of maltreatment is a Child who receives treatment that is not in accordance with the rights of the Child. 29. Village is a legal Community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage Government affairs, the interests of the local Community, based on Community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights recognized and respected in the Government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 30. Child in need of Special Protection is a Child in an emergency situation, a Child in conflict with the law, a Child from an isolated indigenous community, a Child who is economically and/or sexually exploited, a Child victim of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other active substance abuse (Napza), a Child victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, a Child victim of physical and/or psychological Violence, a Child with special needs, and a Child victim of maltreatment and neglect. 31. Child Trafficking is a criminal act or action that meets one or more elements of recruitment, transfer, handover of a Child by using Violence or threat of violence, fraud, kidnapping, confinement, abuse of power, exploitation of a position of vulnerability or debt bondage for the purpose and/or resulting in exploiting the Child. 32.

Article 12

The Regional Government shall provide Women Protection in the form of:
a. prevention of Violence against Women;
b. provision of services for Women victims of Violence requiring coordination at the Regional level; and
c. strengthening and developing institutions providing Women Protection services.

CHAPTER VII SAFE HOUSES

Article 46

1. Women and Children who are victims of Violence requiring ongoing handling have the right to stay in a safe house.
2. The safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall provide a temporary safe place or shelter for victims of Violence until the victim's rights are restored. (3) The operation and management of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that performs functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
4. Further provisions regarding the operation of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 4

The regulation regarding Women Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:
a. guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of every Woman and Child to survival, growth and development;
b. improve the quality of life of Women, Children and family quality;
c. enhance institutional capacity for Women Empowerment and Child Protection in the Region, including the development of gender and Child data systems; and
d. provide protection of Women's rights and fulfillment of Children's Rights including Special Protection for Children from various forms of Violence and other discriminatory treatment.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by "respect for human rights" is that the protection and empowerment of women is carried out as a manifestation of respect for women as part of Human Rights.

Point b rights What is meant by "gender equality" is one of the basic rights as a human being, the right to live with dignity, free from fear and free to determine life choices is not only intended for men, women also have the same rights in essence.

Point c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward Children by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups, and the condition of the Child.

Point d What is meant by "justice and legal certainty" is that in implementing the protection and empowerment of women it is based on justice and legal certainty of equality between men and women. Point e What is meant by "benefit" is to provide the widest possible benefit for children and women for the interests of society, nation and state.

Point f What is meant by "participatory" is that every member of society is encouraged to play an active role in the decision-making process and implementation of child protection and women's empowerment, either directly or indirectly.

Point g What is meant by "the best interests of the Child" is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the Regional Government, parents/family, and the Community, the best interests of the Child must be the primary consideration.

Article 45

1. Special Protection for Children who are victims of mistreatment and neglect as referred to in Article 36 letter i shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment and rehabilitation.
2. Every person and/or any party is prohibited from placing, allowing, involving, ordering the involvement of Children in situations of mistreatment and neglect as referred to in paragraph (1).

CHAPTER XVII

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 57

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, Regional policies concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Region that already exist shall remain in force, insofar as they do not conflict with this Regional Regulation.

Article 39

1. Special Protection for Children from isolated indigenous communities as referred to in Article 36 letter c shall be carried out through the provision of facilities and infrastructure to be able to enjoy their own culture, acknowledge and practice their own religion, and use their own language.
2. Every person and/or any parties are prohibited from obstructing Children as referred to in paragraph (1) from enjoying their own culture, acknowledging and practicing their religion, and using their own language without neglecting access to Community and cultural development.

Article 42

1. Special Protection for Children who are victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking as referred to in Article 36 letter f shall be carried out through supervision, protection, prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and reintegration efforts by the Regional Government and the Community.
2. To implement prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government together with the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, Community, NGOs and Social Organizations shall take steps in the form of:
a. conducting socialization and/or campaigns on the prevention, handling and elimination of Child Trafficking practices;
b. conducting cooperation with other Regions as well as with other countries through bilateral or multilateral cooperation in accordance with the laws and regulations.
3. Protection for Children who are victims of Child Trafficking shall be implemented through Shelters and/or other Child Protection Institutions, through referrals from government institutions or the Community.
4. Every Child who is a victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, has the right to obtain physical, psychological treatment and rehabilitation and reintegration in the family environment and the Community.

Article 44

1. Special Protection for Children with special needs as referred to in Article 36 letter h shall be carried out through efforts to:
a. treat Children humanely in accordance with the dignity and Rights of the Child;
b. fulfill special needs; and
c. obtain equal treatment with other Children to achieve full social integration and individual development as much as possible.
2. Every person and/or any party is prohibited from treating Children with special needs in a discriminatory manner, by disregarding their views including labeling and equalization in education for Children with special needs.

Article 40

1. Special Protection for Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 36 letter d shall be carried out through:
a. prevention of Children from being utilized by certain parties as objects of exploitation through supervision;
b. disseminating and/or socializing laws and regulations related to Protection of Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually;
c. monitoring, reporting and imposing sanctions; and
d. involving various government agencies, companies, labor unions, NGOs, and the Community in the elimination of exploitation of Children.
2. Every person and/or any party is prohibited from conducting economic and/or sexual exploitation of Children as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 20

Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing the fulfillment of Women's rights as referred to in Article 13 shall be stipulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 47

1. The Village Government shall implement Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Village.

Article 40

1. Special Protection for Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 36 letter d shall be carried out through:
a. prevention of Children from being utilized by certain parties as objects of exploitation through supervision;
b. disseminating and/or socializing laws and regulations related to Protection of Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually;
c. monitoring, reporting and imposing sanctions; and
d. involving various government agencies, companies, labor unions, NGOs, and the Community in the elimination of exploitation of Children.

Article 45

Article 44

1. Special Protection for Children with special needs as referred to in Article 36 letter h shall be carried out through efforts to:
a. treat Children humanely in accordance with the dignity and Rights of the Child;
b. fulfill special needs; and
c. obtain equal treatment with other Children to achieve full social integration and individual development as much as possible.
2. Every person and/or any party is prohibited from treating Children with special needs in a discriminatory manner, by disregarding their views including labeling and equalization in education for Children with special needs.

Article 39

Article 26

1. Placement of Children in temporary shelters as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter c shall be carried out if based on the results of identification it is known that:
a. the safety of the Child is threatened;
b. the Child has no family/caregiver or guardian; and
c. the Child cannot be reunited with family/caregiver/guardian and/or the Community.
2. Placement as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be carried out for a certain period of time while the Child receives recovery services and/or until the family/caregiver/guardian is deemed to have the readiness to care for and protect the Child.
3. In the placement as referred to in paragraph (2), the Child shall receive services for the fulfillment of basic needs and psychosocial assistance.
4. The SKPD responsible for social affairs must provide temporary shelters.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tanah Bumbu Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Agency is the Regional Apparatus that organizes government affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection. 6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in organizing government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that Women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 8. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into men and Women. 9. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person recognized by law as a Woman. 10. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a Child who is still in the womb. 11. Child in conflict with the law (ABH) is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child who is a victim of a criminal act and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 13. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting Women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security. 16. Toddler is a Child aged 0 (zero) to 5 (five) years, in the early stages of human development. 17. School-Age Child is a Child aged 6 (six) to 18 (eighteen) years. 18. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs for mental and religious guidance as well as clothing, food, shelter, health, education, physical, and social services are not properly met. 19. Child who is a victim of Violence is a Child who experiences mistreatment such as being abused, humiliated, which endangers the Child physically, mentally and socially. 20. Child maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over the child, who should be trusted, namely parents, close family, teachers, supervisors, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions (World Health Organization). 21. Child in emergency situation is a Child who is in a situation and condition that endangers them such as a Child victim of riots, a Child who becomes a refugee, a Child victim of natural disasters and a Child in armed conflict. 22. Child in conflict with the law is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child victim of a criminal act, and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 23. Child of isolated indigenous community is a Child who lives in a situation of isolation where they cannot access basic needs. 24. Economically exploited Child is a Child who is forced and/or deceived to be employed by parents or others, whether unpaid or paid. 25. Sexually exploited Child is the use of a Child for sexual purposes with cash or other forms of compensation between the Child, buyer of sexual services, intermediary or agent and other parties who profit from the sexual trade of the Child. 26. Child who is a victim of Napza abuse is a Child who suffers from dependence on Napza caused by Napza abuse, either by their own will or because of encouragement or coercion by others. 27. Child with special needs is a Child who experiences physical and/or mental disabilities that interfere with growth and development in accordance with the stages of Child development. 28. Child victim of maltreatment is a Child who receives treatment that is not in accordance with the rights of the Child. 29. Village is a legal Community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage Government affairs, the interests of the local Community, based on Community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights recognized and respected in the Government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 30. Child in need of Special Protection is a Child in an emergency situation, a Child in conflict with the law, a Child from an isolated indigenous community, a Child who is economically and/or sexually exploited, a Child victim of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other active substance abuse (Napza), a Child victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, a Child victim of physical and/or psychological Violence, a Child with special needs, and a Child victim of maltreatment and neglect. 31. Child Trafficking is a criminal act or action that meets one or more elements of recruitment, transfer, handover of a Child by using Violence or threat of violence, fraud, kidnapping, confinement, abuse of power, exploitation of a position of vulnerability or debt bondage for the purpose and/or resulting in exploiting the Child. 32.

Article 5

1. Women Empowerment and Child Protection regulated in this Regional Regulation is an inseparable part of regional development planning in the regional long-term development plan, regional medium-term development plan, and Regional Government work plan whose content concerns Women Empowerment and Child Protection in the Region.

2. Regional development planning as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be set forth in programs and activities for Women Empowerment and Child Protection by referring to the classification, codification, and nomenclature of development planning.

CHAPTER VI

CHILD PROTECTION

Part One General

Article 21

1. The Regional Government shall carry out Child Protection in the Region.
2. Child Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be through the Protection of Children's Rights.
3. Children's Rights as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be guided by the provisions of Regional Regulation of Tanah Bumbu Regency Number 11 of 2021 concerning the Implementation of a Child-Friendly Regency (Regional Gazette of Tanah Bumbu Regency Year 2021 Number 11, Supplement to the Regional Gazette of Tanah Bumbu Regency Number 126).

CHAPTER IX

FAMILY QUALITY

Article 48

1. The Regional Government is obliged to improve family quality in the form of:
a. improving family quality in realizing gender equality and Child Rights.
b. strengthening and developing service provider institutions for improving family quality in realizing gender equality and Child Rights whose working area is within the Region.
c. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and Child Rights whose working area is within the Region.
2. Provisions regarding procedures for improving family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 42

1. Special Protection for Children who are victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking as referred to in Article 36 letter f shall be carried out through supervision, protection, prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and reintegration efforts by the Regional Government and the Community.
2. To implement prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government together with the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, Community, NGOs and Social Organizations shall take steps in the form of:
a. conducting socialization and/or campaigns on the prevention, handling and elimination of Child Trafficking practices;
b. conducting cooperation with other Regions as well as with other countries through bilateral or multilateral cooperation in accordance with the laws and regulations.
3. Protection for Children who are victims of Child Trafficking shall be implemented through Shelters and/or other Child Protection Institutions, through referrals from government institutions or the Community.
4. Every Child who is a victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, has the right to obtain physical, psychological treatment and rehabilitation and reintegration in the family environment and the Community.
